places.quote: this bleak place overgrown with nettles was the churchyard
places.note: Dickens's Cooling churchyard is unnamed in text; generic term used, so treat as fictional marsh churchyard

places.quote: the dark flat wilderness beyond the churchyard, intersected with dikes and mounds and gates
places.note: unnamed marsh country; approximate location only

places.quote: the low leaden line beyond was the river
places.note: river unnamed in passage; identification is inferred

places.quote: the distant savage lair from which the wind was rushing was the sea

places.normalized: Battery at the Thames marshes, Kent
places.quote: You bring the lot to me, at that old Battery over yonder.
places.note: fictional-ish battery; location not fixed in text

places.quote: one of these was the beacon by which the sailors steered
places.note: object, not named place; may be omitted
